title: Regional failover dress-rehearsal and adaptive load-shedding calibration
creator: Samira Chen
description: Goal: Run a controlled, repeatable dress rehearsal that validates multi-region failover behavior, circuit-breaker thresholds, and adaptive load-shedding under simultaneous stress: region loss, GPU pool exhaustion, and dependent service blackholes. Outcomes: calibrated CB thresholds, validated rollback and fallback flows, documented observability gaps, and a runnable runbook for on-call. This ticket covers design, infra changes, test execution window, and post-run analysis. Artifacts include the test matrix, dashboards, GitHub PR for traffic router changes, and the runbook in Confluence.

test_steps: Step 0: Pre-checks: ensure staging telemetry parity, SLO dashboards show baseline, reserve rollback window and on-call engineers.

Step 1: Region fencing - simulate control-plane isolation for us-east-1 by toggling region-fence flag in traffic-router (percentage: 10% -> 30% -> 100%). Monitor reroute latencies and ensure fallback model variants are selected.

Step 2: GPU pool exhaustion - in Dedicated test cluster, spin synthetic inference workers to saturate GPU pool memory and queue depth. Validate admission control triggers and shed policy (reject vs degrade).

Step 3: Dependency blackhole - apply iptables rules on proxy layer to simulate 503s/connection timeouts to external logging/metrics and to private dependency endpoints used by the tokenizer microservice. Verify circuit breaker's trip threshold and fallback cache usage.
Step 4: Combined scenario - run region fence and GPU exhaustion concurrently for 15 minutes while gradually increasing client QPS to observe interaction effects and cascading failures.
Step 5: Recovery choreography - remove the faults in reverse order, validate graceful rejoin of GPU pool, cache warmup, and traffic rebalancing without violating SLOs more than planned error budget.
Step 6: Post-run validation - run synthetic prompts and evaluation harness to detect model quality regressions introduced by fallback variants; export token-level cost and latency traces.
abort_criteria: SLO windows: availability drop > 0.5% for more than 10 minutes beyond planned budget.
P99 latency degradation exceeding 2x baseline for more than 5 minutes and not trending back down after mitigations.
Uncontrolled error surge in control plane (>5% error rate to routing API) or critical alerts from control-plane health checks.
On-call requests an immediate stop for any safety or customer-impact reason.
slo_targets: Hosted API availability target: 99.95% (monthly), planned temporary erosion allowance for rehearsal: 0.2%
P99 latency target (generation): <= 600ms for standard offering; expected transient increase allowed during planned window up to 1.2s
Tail error budget policy: if error budget consumed > 40% during first 30m, abort and rollback.
observability_gaps: No per-model GPU queue depth metric emitted from Dedicated pools (tracked ENG-62100).
Missing distributed trace correlation id for fallback cache hits in the tokenizer path.
Alert thresholds for circuit-breaker trips are coarse; need per-region thresholds.
No synthetic traffic tag applied to distinguish rehearsal traffic from real traffic in billing pipeline.
notes: This rehearsal intentionally tests interaction effects between three failure modes. The focus is not to maximize blast radius but to exercise unexpected coupling (eg. circuit hysteresis causing traffic storms). Engineering leads should be ready to toggle fallback variants and CB limits from the emergency console. After the run we will publish calibrated thresholds and submit follow-ups for instrumentation gaps.
